pinned.hashSource: Microsoft .NET 10.0 release metadata (releases.json / release notes), aspnetcore 10.0.10 windows-hosting-bundle entry. Microsoft publishes SHA-512 for .NET runtime downloads.

notes: This file is the repository-controlled authority for which Hosting Bundle a release pins. It is reviewed like any other source change: edit, commit, tag, publish. A release build never resolves 'latest', so rebuilding the same source release consumes the same runtime bytes.

TWO HASHES, TWO JOBS. 'pinned.expectedHash' is MICROSOFT's published digest in MICROSOFT's algorithm (SHA-512), and answers only: did we download what Microsoft published? Everything downstream - chunk digests, the reassembled-file digest, component integrity - is ITAdmin's own distribution integrity in ITAdmin's own algorithm (SHA-256), and answers: did the upstream-verified bytes reach this server intact? Neither substitutes for the other.

The binary is NEVER committed to ordinary source history. The publisher downloads it from 'pinned.sourceUrl', verifies it against 'pinned.expectedHash', and only then chunks it into the release's Git distribution ref. The server acquires it over the same read-only deploy-key trust path it uses for the application.

Because the installer exceeds the practical per-object limit of a Git host, it is stored as ordered 32 MiB chunks. Each chunk carries its own SHA-256; the REASSEMBLED file must match the distribution SHA-256 before it is executed. The upstream SHA-512 is preserved in the distribution manifest for provenance and later audit.
Do not replace the SHA-512 with a hand-derived SHA-256. The point of pinning the vendor's own algorithm and value is that the pin can be compared against what the vendor actually published.
IIS features must be installed before the Hosting Bundle so ANCM registers with IIS; if IIS was added later, the installer repairs the bundle.
majorVersion/minimumVersion refer to the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework (TFM), not the ANCM DLL file-version major (which may be 20.x).
